paper.title: Learning to Detect an Odd Restless Markov Arm with a Trembling Hand

settings.name_in_paper: Odd arm identification in a restless multi-armed bandit with Markov arms (unknown TPMs), trembling hand
unmapped: Goal is to identify the odd arm: one arm has TPM P1, all others share TPM P2 != P1; fixed-confidence (error probability <= epsilon for all configurations), expected stopping time
Each arm is an ergodic finite-state Markov chain; observations are noiseless states; arms are restless
Trembling hand: intended arm pulled w.p. 1-eta, uniformly random arm w.p. eta (eta>0), the actually pulled arm is observed
TPMs P1, P2 unknown to the learner
Initial states X_0^a ~ phi, a known full-support distribution
settings.definition_quote: Consider a multi-armed bandit with $K\geq 3$ arms ... discrete-time Markov process $\{X_t^a:t\geq 0\}$ associated with arm $a$ that is time-homogeneous, ergodic and takes values in a common finite set $\mathcal{S}$. ... Let the TPM of one of the arms (the {\em odd} arm) be $P_1$, and that of each non-odd arm be $P_2$, where $P_2\neq P_1$. ... A decision entity that knows neither $P_1$ nor $P_2$ wishes to find the odd arm index as quickly as possible while keeping the probability of its decision error small.

source.label: prop:policy_satisfies_desried_error_probability
source.quote: Fix an error probability $\epsilon>0$. If $L=1/\epsilon$, then $\pi^{\star}(L,\delta)\in\Pi(\epsilon)$ for all $\delta>0$.

results.notes: The proof shows the error probability is at most 1/L. The assumptions are stated globally before the Section IV results. 'probability' field chosen loosely; this bounds the error probability itself.

symbols.L_thr: threshold parameter L of the policy (stop when M >= log((K-1)L)); L = 1/epsilon gives error <= epsilon

conditions: Assumption 2: all TPMs lie in P(bar_eps*) with mutually absolutely continuous rows

source.label: prop:almost_sure_upper_bound_for_policy
source.quote: Suppose that $C=(h, P_1, P_2)$ is the underlying arms configuration. For all $\delta>0$, the stopping time of policy $\pi^\star(L,\delta)$ satisfies \limsup_{L\to\infty} \frac{\tau(\pi^\star(L,\delta))}{\log L} \leq \frac{(1+\delta)^2}{R^*(h, P_1, P_2)} almost surely.

results.notes: Almost-sure bound on the stopping time.

symbols.L_thr: threshold parameter L of the policy; L = 1/epsilon gives error <= epsilon

conditions: Assumption 2: all TPMs lie in P(bar_eps*) with mutually absolutely continuous rows

source.label: prop:upper_bound
source.quote: Fix $\delta>0$. Under the arms configuration $C=(h, P_1, P_2)$, the expected stopping time of the policy $\pi=\pi^{\star}(L,\delta)$ satisfies \limsup_{L \to \infty} \frac{E^\pi[\tau(\pi)|C]}{\log L} \leq \frac{(1+\delta)^2}{R^*(h, P_1, P_2)}.

results.notes: With L = 1/epsilon (Proposition 4), this bounds the expected stopping time by (1+delta)^2 log(1/epsilon)/R* asymptotically.

symbols.L_thr: threshold parameter L of the policy; L = 1/epsilon gives error <= epsilon

conditions: Assumption 2: all TPMs lie in P(bar_eps*) with mutually absolutely continuous rows

source.label: prop:main_result
source.quote: Further, under Assumption 1 and Assumption 2, the policy $\pi^\star(L, \delta)$ satisfies the asymptotic upper bound \limsup_{\delta\downarrow 0} \limsup_{L\to\infty}\frac{E^{\pi^\star(L, \delta)}[\tau(\pi^\star(L, \delta))|C]}{\log L}\leq \frac{1}{R^*(h, P_1, P_2)}. Under these assumptions, we therefore have \lim_{\epsilon\downarrow 0}\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\epsilon)}\frac{E^\pi[\tau(\pi)|C]}{\log(1/\epsilon)}=...=\frac{1}{R^*(h, P_1, P_2)}.

results.notes: The lower-bound part of Theorem 1 restates Proposition 1 (r1). Together they show asymptotic optimality, with the limit equal to 1/R*, under the assumptions.
